items.text: Fortnum & Mason, 181 Piccadilly, since 1707. On the hour, look up: above the door the founders, four feet tall, bow to each other. The shop also claims to have invented the Scotch egg in 1738.
Hatchards has sold books on Piccadilly since 1797 and calls itself the oldest bookshop in the UK. Oscar Wilde signed books at the ground-floor table now known as 'Oscar's table'.
Fouquet's, 99 Champs-Élysées, founded in 1899 and a listed historic monument since 1990. Every year the dinner after France's César film awards is held here. Red carpet optional.
Le Procope, 13 rue de l'Ancienne Comédie. A café opened here in 1686; Voltaire and Rousseau came, and Franklin and Jefferson met in it. The old café closed in 1872, today's restaurant opened in 1957.

Botín, Calle de Cuchilleros 17. Guinness lists it as the world's oldest restaurant, and the flame in its oven is never allowed to go out. Historians still argue about the founding date; the oven doesn't care.
Chocolatería San Ginés, Pasadizo de San Ginés 5, has served chocolate con churros since 1894. Galdós and Valle-Inclán both put it in their books.
Babington's, Piazza di Spagna 23. Two young Englishwomen opened this tea room in 1893 with 100 pounds of savings. Its English-language sign stayed up through the Second World War.
Café Central, Herrengasse 14, since 1876. In January 1913 Freud, Tito and Stalin were all customers here. Chess players called the first floor 'the chess school'.

Demel, Kohlmarkt 14, confectioner to the Habsburg court from 1874. In 1954 Hotel Sacher sued it over the 'Original Sacher-Torte'; since 1963 Demel's cake carries an 'Eduard-Sacher-Torte' seal. Cake diplomacy.
U Fleků, Křemencova 11, brewing since 1499 and called Prague's oldest brewery. Its dark 13° lager is brewed on site and sold nowhere else; the halls seat 1,200.
Café Louvre, Národní 22, opened in 1902. Franz Kafka, Albert Einstein and Karel Čapek are on its list of guests.

Gerbeaud, Vörösmarty tér 7. Henrik Kugler started the business in 1858 and moved here in 1870, when the square was Gizella tér. In 1884 he invited a confectioner from Geneva, Emil Gerbeaud. The name stuck.

New York Café, Erzsébet körút 9–11, opened in 1894 in the New York Life Insurance building. Legend says writers threw its front-door key into the Danube so it could never close. The key is still missing.
Livraria Bertrand, Rua Garrett 73–75, has sold books since 1732. Guinness World Records calls it the oldest operating bookstore in the world.
A Brasileira, Rua Garrett 120, opened on 19 November 1905. The bronze Fernando Pessoa outside (Lagoa Henriques, 1988) has had the same terrace seat ever since and has never once ordered.
Brettos in Plaka, founded by Michail Brettos in 1909, is Athens' oldest distillery. Its own ouzo and liqueurs follow recipes traced back to Smyrna; the wall of coloured bottles greets you first.
KaDeWe opened on 27 March 1907 and is called Europe's second-largest department store after Harrods, with over 60,000 m² of shop floor. Pace yourself.
Konnopke's Imbiss, Schönhauser Allee 44b. Max Konnopke started selling sausages in 1930 and opened this stand in 1960; it is known as Berlin's oldest imbiss.
Neuhaus began in these royal galleries in 1857 as an apothecary. In 1912 Jean Neuhaus invented the praline, and in 1915 he and his wife Louise Agostini created the ballotin box.
Delirium Café, Impasse de la Fidélité. In January 2004 Guinness recorded 2,004 beer brands on its list, a world record. Reading the menu counts as a hobby.
Café Hoppe, Spui 18–20, open since 1670. Number 18 is the 'standing Hoppe': you drink on your feet and talk to whoever is next to you.
Tivoli opened on 15 August 1843, the world's second-oldest operating amusement park. Its wooden coaster from 1914 still carries an operator who brakes so it doesn't go too fast.
Den Gyldene Freden in Gamla stan opened in 1722, and the street around it has hardly changed since. Its early fame came from the songs of Carl Michael Bellman.
Bewley's has been on Grafton Street since 1927. Its six Harry Clarke stained-glass windows belong to the building: the courts ruled in 2024, and again in 2026, that they cannot be sold off.
The Brazen Head, 20 Lower Bridge Street, says it dates back to 1198. James Joyce mentions it in Ulysses. The walls know more stories than the menu.
Karl Ernst Wedel founded his chocolate company in 1851, and in 1894 it moved its main factory to this street, Szpitalna. Ptasie Mleczko is still its flagship product.
This kafana is called '?'. In 1892 the owner wanted to name it 'By the Cathedral Church'; the church objected, so he hung a question mark on the door. It stuck. The building dates from 1823.
El Fishawy, in Khan el-Khalili, opened in 1797 and is open 24 hours a day. Naguib Mahfouz was among the writers who came here.

Thorn Tree Café, Stanley Hotel (1902). Travellers pinned notes for each other to the thorns of an acacia here, and people still leave messages. Today's tree dates from 1997. You're doing the digital version.
Shibuya 109 opened in April 1979. The name is a pun: 10 is 'tō' and 9 is 'kyū', as in Tōkyū, and the numbers also matched its 10 a.m. to 9 p.m. hours.
Din Tai Fung started on Xinyi Road in 1958 selling cooking oil. Around 1970 half the shop switched to xiaolongbao, folded 18 times each; by 1972 it was a full restaurant.
Jay Fai, 327 Maha Chai Road: one chef at the wok, ski goggles on. The kitchen earned a Michelin star in the first Bangkok guide, and the crab omelette is the famous dish.
Raffles Hotel opened in 1887. In its Long Bar, bartender Ngiam Tong Boon invented the Singapore Sling, and guests drop peanut shells on the floor on purpose.
Indian Coffee House, Connaught Place. When the Coffee Board planned to close its cafés in the 1950s, the workers formed co-operatives and kept them running; Delhi's dates from 27 December 1957.
Café Giảng: egg coffee was born here in the late 1940s. Milk was scarce, so Nguyễn Giảng whisked in egg yolk instead, as his son tells it.
Café Batavia's building, from around the 1830s, is the second-oldest on Fatahillah Square after the old City Hall. Photos of 1930s celebrities and royalty line the main hall.
Casa de los Azulejos: in 1737 a countess had this palace covered in Puebla tiles. Sanborns moved in by 1918, and Orozco painted the mural 'Omniscience' inside in 1925.
Café de Tacuba, on Calle de Tacuba, was founded in 1912 by Dionisio Mollinedo and is one of Mexico's oldest restaurants.
Café Tortoni, Avenida de Mayo 825, since 1858. Borges had a regular table (his wax figure still sits there), and Gardel and Einstein are among its famous guests.
El Ateneo Grand Splendid opened as a theatre in 1919 and became a bookshop in 2000. The café sits on the old stage, and readers sit in the theatre boxes.
La Puerta Falsa, beside the cathedral off Plaza de Bolívar, opened on 16 July 1816: Colombia's oldest restaurant in continuous operation, known for tamales and chocolate with cheese.
Myeongdong Kyoja opened in 1966 as Jangsujang and took its current name in 1978. The menu is four dishes long, and the Michelin Guide Seoul has listed it since 2017.
BeaverTails opened its first stand here in the ByWard Market in 1980. In February 2009 Barack Obama stopped for one, and the 'Obama Tail' was named after the visit.
Old Ebbitt Grill, 675 15th Street NW, traces itself to 1856 and calls itself Washington's oldest bar. Presidents Grant and Andrew Johnson dined here often.
Ben's Chili Bowl, 1213 U Street, opened on 22 August 1958. In 1968 it stayed open past curfew and fed police, firefighters and activists alike.
Hacı Bekir Efendi, Kastamonu Araç'tan gelip 1777'de Bahçekapı'da küçük bir dükkân açtı. Lokum İngilizcede 'Turkish delight' diye tanındı; 1873 Viyana fuarında gümüş madalya aldı.
Kurukahveci Mehmet Efendi 1871'de kahveyi kavurup öğütüp paketleyerek satmaya başladı; o yıllarda çoğu yerde çiğ çekirdek satılırdı. Art Deco dükkân 1932, mimarı Zühtü Başar. Kuyruk da gelenek.
Pandeli Mısır Çarşısı girişinin üst katında, 1660 tarihli binada; hikâyesi 1901'de başlar. Mavi çinili duvarlar, girişte Audrey Hepburn fotoğrafı. Kapıyı kaçırmak kolay: dik taş merdiveni ara.
Vefa Bozacısı 1876'dan beri burada. Vitrinde Atatürk'ün boza içtiği bardak duruyor. Mermer eşik ve ahşap tezgâh da eskisi gibi.
Hacı Abdullah 1888'de Karaköy iskelesinde açıldı; ruhsatını II. Abdülhamid verdi ve Türkiye'nin resmi kayıtlı ilk lokantası sayılır. 15–20 çeşit kompostosuyla bilinir.
Pera Palace 1895'te Orient Express yolcuları için açıldı ve İstanbul'un ilk elektrikli asansörü buradaydı. Agatha Christie'nin odası anı odası olarak korunuyor.
Baylan 1923'te Beyoğlu'nda Loryan adıyla doğdu, 1934'te Baylan oldu, Kadıköy dükkânı 1961'de açıldı. Kup Griye'yi Harry Lenas yarattı; karamele düşkünlüğümüz için.
